results.summary: Core regulatory facts are confirmed by ZATCA's own site: Wave 24 (SAR 375,000 threshold, deadline 30 June 2026) is officially announced, and ZATCA explicitly does NOT require an accredited/certified provider — any compliant solution qualifies, which removes a key feared barrier for a solo-built tool. Market model is DIRECT: Qoyod's own pricing page confirms real paying customers at SAR 207-379.5/month for a full accounting+e-invoicing suite, proving SMEs already pay for this category; a stripped-down cheaper single-merchant tool has room to undercut. Fine amounts (5,000-50,000 SAR) remain STRONG_INDIRECT only (multiple consistent vendor sources, not an official ZATCA penalty schedule seen directly). Problem-side pain (integration difficulty, no IT staff) is still mostly WEAK vendor-blog evidence, not independently corroborated by user complaints in this session.

results.summary: The regulatory overhaul itself is well corroborated by multiple independent professional/advisory sources (middleeastbriefing, masdareor, KPMG flash alert) converging on the same facts: Yellow tier abolished, 269 profession-level quotas, Qiwa documentation now gating Nitaqat credit from 15 April 2026, wage threshold raised SAR 3,000->4,000. No single official MHRSD primary-source page was fetched in this session, so this stays STRONG_INDIRECT rather than DIRECT. Market-model evidence is weak: only full enterprise HCM suites (Jisr, ZenHR, Bayzat) and EOR/PEO consultancies were found serving this need — no lightweight self-serve SME dashboard product was found, meaning the specific proposed product's market-fit is unproven (a real gap, but also unproven demand at the price point envisioned). Found evidence that GOSI does expose some APIs (contribution/wage data), reducing — but not eliminating — the 'no API access' unknown for a future dashboard.

results.summary: The Mudad/WPS mechanics cited by the candidate are confirmed at DIRECT level via an official Saudi Press Agency (government wire) release: 30-day upload window (down from 60, effective 1 March 2025), reminder cadence, and 20-day inspection trigger all match. This is stronger than the candidate's original 'search snippet' sourcing. The broader claim that HR staff repeat manual work across Qiwa/Mudad/GOSI/Muqeem is only STRONG_INDIRECT (job-ad and vendor-content based; no direct user complaint thread found). Market-model evidence remains weak: existing players (Jisr, ZenHR, Bayzat) are full enterprise HCM suites with no visible micro-business tier or public pricing, so there's no proof a lightweight standalone reminder tool has ever been sold successfully at SME price points. Some official GOSI APIs exist (per DGA inventory), which somewhat de-risks the 'no automation possible' unknown, but ToS/access-process for a solo indie developer is still unverified.
demand_signals: Recurring, ongoing job postings for 'HR Officer – GOSI & HRDF' and 'Government Relations Coordinator' roles (per original discovery, not independently refetched this session)

results.summary: No-show rate figures are confirmed via peer-reviewed sources (PMC/Wiley cross-sectional study at King Abdulaziz Medical City, 21% no-show; MRI department 34.8%), matching the candidate's cited range — but these studies are from large public/military hospitals, not the small private clinics/salons the candidate targets, so the read-across to the target segment is STRONG_INDIRECT at best, not DIRECT. The Fresha commission claim needs correction: Fresha's actual global pricing (Independent ~£14.95/mo single seat; Team ~£9.95/member/mo unlimited seats) shows the 20% commission applies ONLY to new-client bookings sourced via Fresha's own marketplace, not to all bookings or direct-link bookings — the candidate's framing ('20% commission on top of a subscription fee, cutting into thin margins') overstates the universality of the fee, and no Saudi-specific price point was found. Market model is still STRONG_INDIRECT: multiple independent local vendors (OJlinker, Hajzak, Tkana, Watily, Snad) target this exact niche, implying a real and monetizable local market, though none of their pricing/traction was independently verified in this session.
